single_points.text: One reviewer says there is no free jump and you can only jump where a prompt allows it, making everything feel restrictive and scripted.

citation.review_text: I really don't understand the hype for this game. Yes it's very pretty, but It feels terrible to play. Everything feels so restrictive and scripted. The design decisions are puzzling. There's no free jump, you jump only in places where a prompt tells you you are allowed to jump. You can't even drop off a ledge on your own. This makes it feel less like playing a cat and more like playing a trained dog performing a trick. It also makes the very pretty environment feel hollow: you'll see pipes and ledges you could jump to, but there's no prompt, so you can't. You can feel the devs breathing on your neck every step of the way. The chase sequences are awful, you're as railroaded as in the rest of the game so it's endlessly redoing them until you do them "right". No place for going off the beaten track, which is pretty ironic considering you are supposed to be a cat. But at least the kitties are cute I guess...

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the platforming as utilizing pre-configured jump paths selected by the player rather than free-form jumping.

citations.review_text: I loved this game so much. I hope they continue it with a Stray II. The story is really engaging, the puzzles are fun to solve, and being a cat in a platformer makes the whole experience totally novel since you don't have hands to carry things.  I love the mechanic where your jump path is pre-configured and you just select how you want to go.  My hands don't work too well, so games that require a lot of precision and precise timing don't work too well for me.  This one was great though.  The only thing I really wish was different is the ending cutscene could have been longer and shown more of everyone and everything, but maybe it's left mysterious in case they make a sequel.

Purchased for 14,24 euros

I'm a sucker for stories in a post apocalyptic setting and this is a novel take on one of those, what with you being a cat and all. I'm indifferent about cats, by the way, so that wasn't really the draw, but I was curious about how the developers might pull off being a cat in this game. I'm happy to say the cat is indeed very catlike. If you love cats, then you'll be satisfied, I think.

The gameplay consists of very light environmental puzzle solving, platforming and some chase sequences. The platforming is different in that you can't freely jump, but have to look for jump prompts that are attached to surfaces. It doesn't really hinder the freedom of exploration and I got used to it pretty quickly, but it might annoy others. The chase sequences can be a bit random in whether or not the enemies get you, but they're not too hard. Same goes for the puzzle solving, which is fairly straightforward, though I like that the developers chose more subtle signs of where to go and what to do then just slapping the classic yellow paint on everything.

The vibes are great and the world looks amazing, offering varied environments in a constrained setting and really nailing the atmosphere of a post apocalyptic city. They went for a sort of painted photorealism, which fits both the bleakness of what happened in this world and the optimism of the characters that still inhabit it.

The only thing I have a slight problem with is the visual design of the enemies. They're too cute, in my opinion, not really reflecting what they're capable of. It's a minor nitpick, but it took me out of the moment a few times. Silly to say when you're playing a cat with a cute little robot sidekick, but still...

The plot is straightforward and forgettable, but this game is more about environmental storytelling and worldbuilding, which it does adequately. There's enough information to piece together how this world came to be and enough room to use your own imagination…

single_points.text: One reviewer says that the gameplay is quite simple, with automated platforming and puzzles that won't make your brain melt.

citation.review_text:
10 "MEOWS" OUT OF 10. An honest review from a 100% completionist.
 
I'm writing this after unlocking every single achievement — yes, including the one where you have to sleep for over an hour, and the frustrating "Can't Cat-ch Me" run. As someone who has explored every neon-lit corner of this underground world, I can say for sure: Stray is not just a "cat simulator for a couple of evenings." It is a short, incredibly deep, and deeply touching story.
 
What makes this game a masterpiece:
 
• Atmosphere and Visuals. A cyberpunk world where no humans are left, yet humanity remains. The abandoned cities, neon signs, slums, and robots trying to mimic human life — the artists and designers deserve a standing ovation.
 
• Authentic Cat Behaviors. The developers brilliantly captured how cats actually behave. It's genuinely satisfying to knock bottles off ledges, scratch carpets, rub against robots' legs, or just curl up into a ball and sleep to the music. The dedicated "Meow" button is the best mechanic in video game history.
 
• Story and Lore. The journey of B-12 and the stray cat is captivating. Behind a simple beginning lies a sad drama about a lost world, environmental collapse, and hope. The ending leaves a powerful, melancholic aftertaste.
 
A small critique (to be completely honest):
 
Gameplay-wise, it is quite simple. The platforming is automated (you can't miss a jump or fall off a ledge accidentally), and the puzzles won't make your brain melt. But Stray shines through immersion and emotion rather than difficulty.
 
Who is it for?
 
Everyone. If you love cats, appreciate a thick post-apocalyptic atmosphere, and want a beautiful aesthetic experience — get it without hesitation. For me, it's one of the most memorable and soulful gaming adventures in recent years.
 
Bottom line: a short, soulful game that's easy to recommend. Highly recommended! 🐾

single_points.text: One reviewer says that playing with a keyboard and mouse involves way too much key mashing and recommends using a controller instead.

citation.review_text: A glorious game, but one you'll definitely need a controller for. I tried a play through with K&M (before my first controller), and had to abandon 5 hours in. Way too much key mashing, and I had no opportunity to take in the gorgeous surroundings. However, with a controller it definitely hits the spot for me. I'm a dog person, but I definitely fell for Stray, as I did for the story and each of the characters. Loved finding the memories, and the pure relaxing pleasure of it all motivated me to complete. I'm looking forward to getting back to it once I've cleared my backlog.
